judged_text: Attendee rows are persisted via prisma.booking.update before updateCalendarAttendees runs, and the write is not rolled back if the calendar update fails. If the calendar provider errors, the response is a 500 but the attendees remain in the DB; a user retrying re-enters the handler where the dedup filter now rejects those emails, so the calendar event is permanently missing the guests even though the UI shows them added — a silently divergent copy of the attendee set between DB and calendar.

record.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Attendee rows are persisted via prisma.booking.update before updateCalendarAttendees runs, and the write is not rolled back if the calendar update fails. If the calendar provider errors, the response is a 500 but the attendees remain in the DB; a user retrying re-enters the handler where the dedup filter now rejects those emails, so the calendar event is permanently missing the guests even though the UI shows them added — a silently divergent copy of the attendee set between DB and calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no transaction/rollback or try/catch around the calendar update. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation fails (500) but the DB write remains. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees`, so those previously persisted guests will be rejected (`uniqueGuests.length === 0` => BAD_REQUEST), preventing a re-sync and leaving the calendar missing guests while the DB/UI shows them added.
